data.title: Lockerbie bombing trial delayed over ‘new evidence’
data.description: WASHINGTON - A US federal judge has postponed the trial of a Libyan man accused of making the bomb that destroyed a Pan Am flight over Scotland in 1988, killing 270 people, citing new evidence.

data.title: ‘Traumatic’ tornado shatters French village
data.description: POMAS, France - Two people were in critical condition and thousands of households were without power on Tuesday after a “tornado of severe intensity” wreaked havoc in southern France, officials said.

data.title: Trees 'giving up': climate change hammers historic English gardens
data.description: HAMPTON COURT (UNITED KINGDOM) - At Hampton Court Palace, head gardener Graham Dillamore strode across the burnt beige grass in the spectacular formal gardens southwest of London, laid out in the 17th century.

data.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
data.description: WINDHOEK — Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

data.title: Florida opens a dedicated Jellyfish Museum
data.description: Right on the coast of Florida, Pompano Beach has opened a new venture dedicated to one of the ocean’s most enigmatic creatures: the jellyfish, a boneless and brainless invertebrate that has survived in the earth’s ocean for over 500 million years.

data.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

data.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
data.description: TOKYO — Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.

data.title: Trump veers from boredom to denial after six months of Iran war
data.description: WASHINGTON — At an impromptu press conference last week, US President Donald Trump waxed lyrical about his helipad, his ballroom and his granite paving stones.

data.title: Families of detained Chinese Christians cling to faith in legal limbo
data.description: BEIHAI — Clasping her hands together in prayer, four-year-old Huanle tells God she misses her mum, whom she has not seen since Chinese authorities raided their home last year in a crackdown on their unregistered church.

data.title: Tens of thousands flee fire near US city of Reno
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Tens of thousands of people looked set to spend another night away from home Monday as a wind-driven fire bore down on the western US city of Reno.

data.title: US proposes expanding UN Sudan arms embargo to entire country
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The United States proposed at the UN on Monday to expand an arms embargo on the Sudanese region of Darfur to cover all of Sudan, saying the nation's brutal conflict risks regional expansion.

data.title: Ceasefire verification mission heads to east DR Congo
data.description: KINSHASA - A mission to verify a fragile ceasefire between the Congolese army and Rwanda-backed M23 armed group was deployed Monday to the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the two sides traded accusations of abuse.

data.title: US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The United States on Monday removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions and marking another step in warming ties between the countries.

data.title: Trump says to double tariffs on Canada autos as trade fight heats up
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Monday that he would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles beginning next year, as the neighboring countries spiral towards an escalating trade war.

data.title: France readies high school phone ban for next month
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The French government said Monday it would press ahead with a ban on mobile phones in high schools from next month, but trade unions warned that the measure might be hard to implement quickly.

data.title: French poll shows Le Pen's biggest challenger may be hard left's Melenchon
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon may have the best chance of reaching the run-off against far-right leader Marine Le Pen in next spring's election, a new poll showed Monday, underscoring the increasingly polarised nature of the race.

data.title: Empire State Building climbers kiss outside court after viral proposal
data.description: NEW YORK - A couple who climbed to the top of the Empire State Building and got engaged appeared in a New York court Monday, before giving each other a lingering kiss in full view of the world's media.

data.title: British PM Burnham hits a chord on Kyiv visit
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Monday strummed on a guitar and also went to a shopping mall destroyed by a Russian strike as he visited Kyiv to show his country's support for Ukraine.

data.title: Saudi Arabia to invest $7 bn in theme parks near Paris: French presidency
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding for a six-billion-euro ($7 billion) Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, including one likely to be manga-themed, the office of the French president said.

data.title: Trump claims Iran 'collapsing' as US threatens 'economic D-Day'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was "collapsing" as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

data.title: Despair and anger in Conakry after deadly landfill collapse
data.description: CONAKRY - Abou Hamza, an outraged resident of the Dar es Salam neighbourhood of Conakry where a landfill collapse killed 30 people over the weekend, said that locals had tried to warn Guinea's authorities about the danger.

data.title: OSCE says Kazakh elections lacked choice
data.description: ALMATY (KAZAKHSTAN) - Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections were marred by a lack of "political choice", according to the Organisation for Security and Co-operation (OCSE) on Monday, after the ruling party won in a landslide.

data.title: Kremlin says UK preventing peace by giving missile info to Ukraine
data.description: MOSCOW - The Kremlin said Monday that the Britain was preventing peace in Ukraine by giving Kyiv information needed to produce SCALP long-range missiles, and threatened to destroy plants manufacturing them.

data.title: Attacks on Red Cross in DR Congo making Ebola fight 'harder'
data.description: GENEVA - The Red Cross voiced alarm on Monday after six workers taking part in a desperate bid to contain a deadly Ebola outbreak were injured in attacks last week in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

data.title: Malaysia says Indonesia to open airspace for cloud seeding to tackle haze
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR — Indonesia has given Malaysian agencies ⁠official permission ⁠to enter its ⁠airspace to conduct cloud seeding operations, Malaysia ’s environment minister has said, part of both countries’ efforts to combat the haze blanketing the region.

data.title: New Zealand moves to ban social media for under-16s
data.description: WELLINGTON - New Zealand's government introduced legislation on Monday to ban under 16s from using social media, joining a number of countries seeking to keep youngsters off sites such as Instagram and TikTok.

data.title: Migrants, rescue ships face threats, harassment at sea
data.description: MARSEILLE — A leading aid group said Monday that migrants crossing the Mediterranean and rescue ships that help them face increasing levels of threat and harassment from Libyan groups.

data.title: Syria says Israel talks addressed de-escalation, staying out of Israel-Turkey tensions
data.description: DAMASCUS - Syria said it held talks with Israel in Jordan on Sunday on de-escalation after recent Israeli strikes, and on keeping the country out of tensions between Israel and Turkey, an ally of Damascus.

data.title: Landfill collapse kills 30 in Guinea
data.description: CONAKRY - Thirty people died in Guinea's capital Conakry on Sunday when a mound of rubbish in a landfill collapsed before dawn onto neighbouring homes following heavy rains, the government said.

data.title: Trump admin predicts US trade war 'devastating' for Canada
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The Trump administration on Sunday warned that Canada would be "foolish" to think it could win a trade war with the United States, predicting a "devastating" impact on its northern neighbor.

data.title: Norwegian King Harald's health has 'deteriorated': palace
data.description: OSLO - The health of Norway's 89-year-old King Harald V, in hospital due to complications from a blood condition, has "deteriorated" over the weekend, a statement from the palace said Sunday.

data.title: After Wildberries, Ukraine launches drone campaign on Russia's Ozon
data.description: MOSCOW - Ukraine on Sunday hit a warehouse belonging to Russian e-commerce giant Ozon for the second day running, as Kyiv vowed to expand its attacks on logistics sites.

data.title: Trump caps USA's 250th birthday summer with Indy race through Washington
data.description: WASHINGTON - ​President Donald Trump will cap the celebration of the U.S. 250th ‌anniversary with a first-of-its-kind auto race through the streets of Washington, closing a summer defined by sports and spectacle as drivers speed past some of the capital's most iconic landmarks.

data.title: Zelensky rejects wartime elections, says would 'split' Ukraine
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks made public Sunday that it would be too dangerous for Ukraine to hold an election while it fights Russia's invasion, after a call by his former defence minister to organise a vote.

data.title: Suicidal son takes parents with him in death plunge
data.description: A suicidal teenager and his parents, trying to help him, all died in a fall from a clifftop after a three-hour attempt to persuade the young man to move away from the edge in India's Maharashtra state.

data.title: Thousands expected at Sweden climate demo as election looms
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Around 10,000 people are expected to turn out for a climate demonstration in Stockholm on Sunday, according to Swedish police and organisers, just weeks ahead of a general election where the issue is among voters' top concerns.

data.title: Macron hosts Saudi's MBS for visit ranging from esports to Mideast
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French President Emmanuel Macron welcomes Saudi crown prince and de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day visit set to range from esports to the war in the Middle East.

data.title: DR Congo capital wary of Ebola nightmare
data.description: MALUKU (DR CONGO) - The Ebola virus has spread across Democratic Republic of Congo at a frightening speed and one of the authorities' biggest fears is that it reaches the teeming capital of Kinshasa.

data.title: Teen girl killed in Swedish school sword attack
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Swedish police said a 17-year-old female student was the fatal victim in a sword attack at a high school where widespread tributes were paid Saturday.
